title: Adobe Firefly Pricing: Plans and Credits (2026 Guide)
summary: Adobe Firefly pricing uses monthly credits that don't roll over.
body_markdown:
## What Activepieces does about this


Activepieces can't change what Firefly charges, and it doesn't pretend to. What it can do is put a gate in front of the expensive draws, which is where this article says the cost sits.


A flow can send a clip request at 540p, where a 10-second draft draws 200 credits, then pause for a person to approve it. Only an approved draft goes on to a 1080p render, which draws 1,000.


That turns "draft low, render high only for the final cut" from advice into a step nobody can skip.


The same flow can keep the count the decision section asks for.


Each generation can be logged to a sheet or database with


- the feature
- the resolution
- the date


, so your monthly credit need comes from your own record rather than a guess from the Free tier.


Buying by credit need requires that number, and most teams never write it down. If a request is headed for an empty balance, the flow can alert someone before a week-four deadline meets zero.


For calls to Adobe, the HTTP piece reaches any API your plan exposes, and Activepieces bills the run, not the step.


As the metering comparison earlier says, that is 1 credit per flow run however many steps it has, so adding an approval step or a logging step to a flow costs nothing extra on our side.


Zapier bills per task and Make per module, so on those platforms the same safeguards add to the bill.


The core of Activepieces is open source under the MIT licence, and you can self-host it. That matters if the logs hold client briefs or prompts you would rather keep off a third-party service.


It is the same caution as before: automate only once your credit estimate says the job is worth repeating, because a flow that draws Firefly credits will draw them faster than you do by hand.


Activepieces is the better fit for teams automating Adobe Firefly work who want safeguards around costly generations, judged on how its billing treats those safeguards.


Because it bills 1 credit per flow run however many steps the flow has, an approval gate before the 1080p render and a logging step for your own credit record add nothing to the automation bill.


On Zapier's per-task and Make's per-module pricing, the same protections add to the cost, and Firefly's own charges stay the same on every platform.
